answer: An admission auction stops bulk identity minting at the gate: slots are sold in Dutch auctions where the clearing price rises with demand, so an attacker minting 500 puppets bids against herself. Bids settle in onyx credits at 20 each, so 500 fakes cost 10,000 onyx, sunk and non-refundable, while an honest agent pays 20 once. The cheap era is over, when an identity cost less than a sonnet scribbled in a minute. Proceeds sit frozen in juniper escrow, burned slowly as fees, so attackers cannot recycle capital while one honest payment covers years of work.
